sections.content:
28,305 people

were counted on the census as "window cleaners" in England and Wales in March 2021.
Window cleaners wash and polish windows and other glass fittings.

More men than women had this job

Among people working as "window cleaners" there were more men than women (95.5% compared with 4.5%).

This means "window cleaners" had a different proportion of men and women compared with the wider occupation group it falls within of "elementary administration and service occupations".

Men made up 95.5% and women made up 4.5% of "window cleaners"
Across the whole working population, 52% were men and 48% were women.

Other jobs that had a similar proportion of men and women to "window cleaners" included:

  • aircraft maintenance and related trades
  • TV, video and audio servicers and repairers
  • metal plate workers, smiths, moulders and related occupations

These are the occupations for which the proportion of men and women was most equally split:

  • quality assurance and regulatory professionals
  • chartered and certified accountants
  • conservation professionals

People who had this job were generally older

The occupation of "window cleaners" had an older age profile compared with the whole working population.

The largest age group of people who had this job were those aged 50 to 54 years. Of the whole working population 11.7% were aged 50 to 54 years. For people working as "window cleaners", 14.3% were in this age group.

The age group with the smallest proportion of people working as "window cleaners" was 16 to 19 years.

Other jobs that had a similar age profile to "window cleaners" included:

  • construction and building trades (other)
  • mobile machine drivers and operatives (other)
  • print finishing and binding workers

Select your age group to see the ten most popular occupations for your age

We can look at who worked as "window cleaners" by age group and for men and women at the same time to see how these two factors interact.

There is a higher number of men than women with this occupation across all age groups. The age profile for men and women is shown in the chart below.

The percentage of men and women who are "window cleaners" across age groups

How many people do this job by disability status, employment type and area

Of people working as "window cleaners", 11.8% were disabled. This means people said they had a long-term condition that limited them "a little" or "a lot" in their day-to-day activities. The average for all occupations is 9.6%.

Disability is more common among people who are older. This occupation had an older age profile compared with the whole working population.

People with this job were more likely to work part-time than full-time (55.1% compared with 44.9%).

They are also more likely to be self-employed (82.5%) than an employee (17.5%).

The region of England and Wales with the highest percentage of people with this job was the South East. At a local level, the areas with the highest percentage of people in this occupation included Wigan, this is in the region of the North West.
